files.content: Left page (247v): cipher letter, numeral-group nomenclator, mixed with clear French connective words in the same hand/line -- NOT a separate interlinear gloss (see NOTES.md gloss verdict). Right page (248r): closing only, 'Monseigneur' / 'Vostre tres humble et tres obeissant serviteur' / signed 'Vergier'.

Left page (248v): archival docket 'Mr. Vergier a Boulogne ce 26e mars 1696' at the head, and a second docket on the folded address strip 'Mr. Vergier a Calais ce 20 mars 96 / [Angleterre?]'. Right page (249r): opens 'Monseigneur', dense numeral-group cipher mixed with clear French, continues onto canvas253.

Continuation of the 26 March 1696 letter from canvas252. Both pages dense mixed clear/cipher; names 'Milord Myddleton' (in clear) among cipher groups. Closes 'Je suis avec un profond respect / Monseigneur / Vostre tres humble et tres obeissant serviteur' signed 'Vergier' at the foot of the right page.

A separate cipher letter (not a continuation of the 26 March letter). Right page opens naming 'Mde Pontchartrain' in clear within the running text, mixes cipher groups with clear French discussing Dunkerque armament, M. de Chasteaurenault, Milord Myddleton; closes 'Je suis avec un profond respect / Monteigneur / ... obeissant seruiteur' signed 'Vergier'. Left page continues the same letter (cipher + clear), opening clause references 'M. de Pontchartrain le d[uc?]' and naval postings.
